questions.h: % 10 gives the last digit; / 10 removes it.
questions.e: n % 10 is the last digit (6) and n / 10 drops it (409). Every digit loop is built from these two steps.

questions.q: For n ≥ 1, which formula gives the number of digits of n?
questions.e: log10(100) = 2, so floor + 1 gives 3. ceil(log10(100)) gives 2, which is wrong for every power of 10.

questions.q: This loop should add up all the digits of n (n > 0). Which condition goes in the blank?
questions.h: When should the loop stop: when n has one digit left, or when nothing is left?
questions.e: Keep going until n becomes 0. n > 9 and n >= 10 skip the first digit; n % 10 > 0 stops at the first 0 digit (for example in 105).

questions.q: This code should reverse the digits of n (123 becomes 321). Which expression goes in the blank?
questions.h: Shift rev one place left, then append the last digit of n.
questions.e: rev * 10 makes room at the end, and + n % 10 puts n's last digit there. For 123: 3 → 32 → 321.

questions.q: Which code turns n into its first digit (for example, 4096 becomes 4)?
questions.h: Keep dropping last digits until exactly one digit is left.
questions.e: Stop once n has one digit (n < 10). Looping while n > 0 runs one step too far and ends at 0; n % 10 is the last digit, not the first.

questions.q: This function should return true when n is a palindrome (reads the same backwards, like 121). For n = 121 it returns false. What is the bug?
o: n is 0 after the loop; compare rev with a saved copy of n
% and / are the wrong way round
questions.h: What is the value of n when the loop finishes?
questions.e: The loop destroys n, so rev is compared with 0. Save int orig = n; before the loop and return rev == orig.

questions.q: This loop should add up the digits of n. For n = 47 it never stops. Which line is wrong?
o: sum += n % 10; should be sum += n / 10;
questions.e: n = 47 % 10 = 7, then 7 % 10 = 7 forever. The step that shrinks n must be n /= 10.

questions.q: This function should multiply the digits of n (for 234: 2 × 3 × 4 = 24). It returns 0. What is the fix?
questions.e: A product must start at 1 (a sum starts at 0). With prod = 0 every multiplication stays 0.

questions.q: This function should count the digits of n. What does it return for n = 0?
questions.h: Does the loop run even once when n is 0?
questions.e: The loop never runs, so it returns 0, but 0 has one digit. Handle it first: if (n == 0) return 1;

questions.q: A function adds up the digits of n with a while (n > 0) loop. For n = −123 it returns 0 instead of 6. What is the best fix?
o: Work on llabs(n) stored in a long long
questions.e: Take the absolute value first. With n != 0 the loop runs, but the digits come out negative (−3, −2, −1), so the sum is −6. Use long long because abs(INT_MIN) does not fit in an int.

questions.q: You reverse n = 1999999999 and store the result in an int called rev. What happens?
o: rev overflows (9999999991 > INT_MAX); use long long
questions.h: How big is the reversed number, and what is the largest int?
questions.e: 9999999991 is far above INT_MAX (about 2.1 × 10^9). Store rev in a long long, or check before each step if the problem asks you to detect overflow.

questions.q: What is the time complexity of a loop over the digits of n?
questions.e: The loop runs once per digit, and n has floor(log10 n) + 1 digits. For n = 10^18 that is only 19 steps.

questions.q: How much extra space does reversing n with rev = rev * 10 + n % 10 use?
questions.h: Count the variables, not the digits.
questions.e: Only rev and n are kept, so the space is O(1). Converting n to a string would use O(number of digits) = O(log n).
